name: Baby Poop
lede: Baby Poop is a dark, mustard-olive brown named for the plain color of an infant's stool, one of a cluster of scatological names the 2010 xkcd color survey gave to this same patch of yellow-brown.

sections.title: A crowd name for a plain comparison
sections.body:
The name comes from Randall Munroe's 2010 xkcd color survey, where visitors typed a word next to a swatch and the most common label for each cluster of clicks won [1]. Who typed "baby poop" first for this shade is undocumented; the survey records only the winning name, not its author [1]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the same patch as a light olive, about 3.5 units off, with Munsell notation 5.9Y 5.1/8.1 [1].

The same vote also produced [[baby-poop-green|Baby Poop Green]], a cooler sibling just one step away, and separate entries for [[baby-poo|Baby Poo]], [[baby-shit-brown|Baby Shit Brown]] and [[baby-shit-green|Baby Shit Green]], all naming the same real-world comparison rather than a dye or a place [1]. The closest look-alikes in our data are [[puke-brown|Puke Brown]], about 2.6 units off, and [[hazel|Hazel]], with [[diarrhea|Diarrhea]] and [[poo|Poo]] nearby too [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, finds this mustard-brown in 114 of them, about 0.48 percent, and it is more common than 54 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1700s, at 1.5 times the expected rate for that century (17 of 3,449 paintings from then), and inside a painting it is almost always an accent, 68 percent of the time, by lightness rank rather than raw area [2].

It is also over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.8 times the expected rate [2]. The earliest match in our archive is dated 1480, five hundred and thirty years before the name itself appears in 2010 [2]. Our archive's early centuries are thin, so that date is a floor, not a first, and the match is only a look-alike hue, not proof the name or a matching pigment existed then [2].
